tools.description:
PCB domain router — board lifecycle, footprints, nets, routing, zones, silkscreen.

Operations:

LIFECYCLE
  create(pcb_path)
      -> {status, file}   Create a new empty .kicad_pcb file.

  load(pcb_path)
      -> {status, file, footprint_count, track_count, footprints}
         Load a PCB file and return a summary.

  finalize(pcb_path, fix_silkscreen=True, fill_zones_flag=True)
      -> {status, silkscreen, zones}
         Fix silkscreen overlaps and fill copper zones in one step.

BOARD
  set_outline(pcb_path, x_mm, y_mm, width_mm, height_mm)
      -> {status, previous_edge_cuts_removed, outline}
         Set a rectangular board outline on Edge.Cuts (replaces existing).

  set_design_rules(pcb_path, min_track_width_mm=0.2, min_clearance_mm=0.2,
                   min_via_diameter_mm=0.6, min_via_drill_mm=0.3,
                   min_hole_to_hole_mm=0.25, min_through_hole_diameter_mm=0.3,
                   min_copper_edge_clearance_mm=0.5)
      -> {status, design_rules, project_rules_updated}
         Set PCB design rules in the PCB file and .kicad_pro.

  get_constraints(pcb_path)
      -> {status, board_outline, keepout_zones, design_rules,
          existing_footprints_count, total_keepout_area_mm2}
         Board outline + keepouts + design rules. Shared with audit.constraints.

FOOTPRINTS
  place_footprint(pcb_path, library, footprint_name, reference, value,
                  x_mm, y_mm, rotation_deg=0, layer="F.Cu",
                  check_keepouts=True)
      -> {status, placed, bounding_box, placement_warnings?}

  move_footprint(pcb_path, reference, x_mm, y_mm, rotation_deg=None,
                 check_keepouts=True)
      -> {status, reference, x_mm, y_mm, rotation, placement_warnings?}

  list_footprints(pcb_path)
      -> {status, footprint_count, footprints}

  get_pad_positions(pcb_path, reference)
      -> {status, reference, pad_count, pads}

  get_footprint_dimensions(library, footprint_name, rotation_deg=0)
      -> {status, body_bbox, courtyard?, pad_span, keepout_zones?}
         Query footprint dimensions WITHOUT placing it on a PCB.

NETS
  add_net(pcb_path, net_name)
      -> {status, net, net_code}

  rename_net(pcb_path, old_name, new_name)
      -> {status, old_name, new_name, net_code, replacements}

  list_nets(pcb_path)
      -> {status, net_count, nets}

  set_net_class(pcb_path, class_name, nets, track_width_mm=0.25,
                clearance_mm=0.2, via_diameter_mm=0.6, via_drill_mm=0.3)
      -> {status, class_name, action, nets_assigned}

  assign_pad_net(pcb_path, reference, pad_number, net_name)
      -> {status, reference, pad, net}

  bulk_assign_pad_nets(pcb_path, assignments)
      -> {status, assigned, error_count, nets_created, errors}

ROUTING
  add_trace(pcb_path, start_x_mm, start_y_mm, end_x_mm, end_y_mm,
            trace_width_mm=0.25, layer="F.Cu", net_name="")
      -> {status, trace}

  add_via(pcb_path, x_mm, y_mm, drill_mm=0.3, size_mm=0.6,
          net_name="", via_type="through")
      -> {status, via}

  clear_routing(pcb_path, clear_tracks=True, clear_vias=True,
                clear_zones_flag=False)
      -> {status, tracks_removed, vias_removed, zones_removed}

  edit_trace_width(pcb_path, new_width_mm, net_filter="", layer_filter="")
      -> {status, updated, skipped}

ZONES
  add_zone(pcb_path, net_name, layer="F.Cu", corners=[], clearance_mm=0.3,
           min_width_mm=0.2, connect_pads="thermal", priority=0)
      -> {status, zone}   corners=[] auto-derives from board outline.

  fill_zones(pcb_path)
      -> {status, fill_success, zones_filled, zones}

SILKSCREEN + TEXT
  add_text(pcb_path, text, x_mm, y_mm, layer="F.SilkS",
           text_size_mm=1.0, thickness_mm=0.15, rotation_deg=0)
      -> {status, text, x_mm, y_mm, layer}

  list_silkscreen(pcb_path)

tools.description:
Estimate minimum board dimensions from a list of footprints.

Loads each footprint from KiCad libraries to measure its bounding box,
sums the total component area, applies a routing factor (components
typically need 2-3x their area for routing), and suggests board
dimensions. Use this BEFORE creating the PCB to choose the right
board size and avoid resize iterations.

padding_mm.description: Edge clearance around board perimeter in mm (default 2.0).

routing_factor.description:
Multiplier for total component area to account for
routing space (default 2.5). Use 2.0 for simple boards, 3.0 for
dense designs with many nets.

tools.name: estimate_board_size
tools.title: Estimate Board Size

tools.description:
Suggest component positions based on net connectivity.

Analyzes the netlist connections between footprints already placed on
the PCB and suggests optimized positions that minimize total trace
length. The most-connected component (usually the MCU) is placed
centrally, and other components are arranged around it based on
connectivity strength.

Does NOT modify the PCB. Returns suggested positions that can be
applied with move_footprint.

Respects board outline and keepout zones. Components with embedded
keepout zones (like ESP32 antenna keepouts) are placed to keep
their keepout areas within the board boundary.

pcb_path.description:
Path to the .kicad_pcb file with footprints placed
and nets assigned (run build_pcb_from_schematic first, or
use pcb(operation="add_net") + pcb(operation="bulk_assign_pad_nets")).

spacing_mm.description: Minimum gap between component courtyards in mm (default 1.0).

footprint_ref.description: Optional: filter to a specific footprint reference (e.g., 'R1', 'U1', 'C3')

net_code.description: Optional: filter to a specific net code

tools.name: get_pads

tools.description: Get the ratsnest (unrouted connections) showing which pads need to be connected. Returns nets with 2+ pads, their connection requirements, and routing status.

net_code.description: Optional: filter to a specific net code

unrouted_only.description: Optional: if true, only return nets that appear to need routing (default: false)

tools.name: get_ratsnest

tools.description: Get design rules (clearances, track widths, via sizes) for all net classes. Essential for knowing valid routing parameters.

net_code.description: Optional: get rules for a specific net's class only

tools.name: get_design_rules

tools.description: Check if a point or track segment would violate clearance rules against existing copper. Use before placing tracks to validate paths.

clearance_mm.description: Optional: override clearance in mm (default: from design rules)

end_x_mm.description: Optional: end X for checking a track segment

end_y_mm.description: Optional: end Y for checking a track segment

net_code.description: Net code of the object being placed (same-net objects are ignored)

tools.name: check_clearance

tools.description: Find a collision-free path between two points using A* pathfinding. Returns waypoints that can be used with place_track.

grid_size_mm.description: Grid resolution in mm (default: 0.5). Smaller = more precise but slower

net_code.description: Net code being routed (same-net objects are not obstacles)

tools.name: find_path

tools.description: Suggest a route between two pads by pad reference (e.g., 'R1-1' to 'C1-2'). Automatically finds pad positions and calculates path.
tools.name: suggest_route

tools.description: Route between two pads using KiCad's Push & Shove router. This is the RECOMMENDED way to route - it automatically avoids obstacles, pushes existing tracks, and maintains DRC clearances.
tools.name: route_pads

tools.description: Get all obstacles on a layer that would block routing. Useful for understanding what's in the way.

net_code.description: Net code being routed (same-net objects excluded)

tools.name: get_obstacles

tools.description: Place a track segment between two points. Returns the track ID if successful.

layer.description: Layer name (e.g., 'F.Cu' for front copper, 'B.Cu' for back copper)

net_code.description: Net code to assign (get from get_nets)

tools.name: place_track

tools.description: Place a via at a specific location to connect between layers
tools.name: place_via

tools.description: Delete a track or via by its ID

item_id.description: The ID of the item to delete (UUID string)

tools.name: delete_item

tools.description: Begin a transaction for multiple changes. Changes won't appear until end_commit is called.
tools.name: begin_commit

tools.description: End a transaction, either committing or dropping all changes since begin_commit

action.description: Whether to commit or drop the changes (default: commit)

tools.name: end_commit

tools.description: Get all wire segments in the schematic. Wires connect component pins and labels.
tools.name: get_schematic_wires

tools.description: Get all labels in the schematic. Labels define net names and connections between wires.

label_type.description: Optional: filter to a specific label type. Local labels connect within a sheet, global labels connect across sheets.

tools.name: get_schematic_labels

tools.description: Get all symbols (components) in the schematic. Returns component references, values, positions (in mils), and library IDs. Use position_mils to get coordinates for wiring.

reference_prefix.description: Optional: filter by reference prefix (e.g., 'R' for resistors, 'C' for capacitors)

tools.name: get_schematic_symbols

tools.description: Get all hierarchical sheets in the schematic. Sheets allow multi-page designs.
tools.name: get_schematic_sheets

tools.description: Get all wire junctions in the schematic. Junctions indicate where wires connect.
tools.name: get_schematic_junctions

tools.description: Get all no-connect symbols in the schematic. No-connects indicate intentionally unconnected pins.
tools.name: get_schematic_no_connects

tools.description: Draw a wire segment between two points in the schematic. Coordinates in mils. Use position_mils from get_symbol_pins to connect to exact pin locations.

start_x.description: Start X coordinate in mils (thousandths of an inch). A4 page is ~11700 x 8300 mils.

tools.name: draw_schematic_wire

tools.description: Add a net label to the schematic. Labels define net names for wires. Coordinates in mils. Place on wire endpoints or pin positions.

label_type.description: Type of label (default: local). Use 'global' for connections across sheets.

x.description: X coordinate in mils (thousandths of an inch). A4 page is ~11700 x 8300 mils.

tools.name: add_schematic_label

tools.description: Get all available symbol libraries. Returns library names, descriptions, and symbol counts. Use this to discover what libraries are available before searching for symbols.
tools.name: get_symbol_libraries

tools.description: Search for symbols across all libraries by name or keyword. Use this to find the right library and symbol name before placing. Example queries: 'resistor', 'op amp', 'MOSFET', 'connector'.
tools.name: search_symbols

tools.description: Place a symbol from a library onto the schematic. Use search_symbols first to find the library and symbol name. Coordinates are in mils (1 mil = 0.0254mm). A4 page is ~11700 x 8300 mils. Center of page is roughly (5850, 4150).

unit.description: Unit number for multi-unit symbols like op amps (default: 1)

tools.name: place_symbol

tools.description: Get all pins of a specific symbol in the schematic. Returns pin names, numbers, positions in mils (position_mils), electrical types, and net connections. Use these mil coordinates directly with draw_schematic_wire to connect pins. Use get_schematic_symbols first to get the symbol ID.
tools.name: get_symbol_pins

tools.description: Update a symbol's position, rotation, or field values (Reference, Value, etc.).
tools.name: update_symbol

tools.description: Auto-annotate all symbols with reference designators (R1, R2, C1, etc.).

reannotate.description: Re-annotate all symbols, even those already annotated (default: false)

tools.name: annotate_symbols

tools.description: Add a symbol (component) to the schematic using s-expression format. This is an advanced tool that requires knowledge of KiCad's s-expression format.

sexpr.description: S-expression string defining the symbol, similar to .kicad_sch file format

tools.name: add_schematic_symbol

tools.description: Delete a schematic item (wire, label, symbol, etc.) by its ID

item_id.description: The ID of the item to delete (UUID string)

tools.name: delete_schematic_item
